summary: A small example plan demonstrating requirement traceability, explicit task outputs, and a dependency graph.

project.name: Sample Inventory API
project.request: Design a small inventory API with item lookup and stock adjustment.

requirements.statement: Clients can retrieve an inventory item by its identifier.
acceptanceCriteria: A known item returns its identifier, name, and available quantity.
An unknown item produces the documented not-found response.

requirements.statement: Stock adjustments preserve an auditable reason and quantity delta.
acceptanceCriteria: Each adjustment records item, delta, reason, actor reference, and timestamp.
Invalid adjustments are rejected according to the documented quantity rules.

requirements.statement: The API must meet a defined latency target under the agreed reference load.

measurement.measurementMethod: Run the agreed load-test profile and capture p95 latency.

acceptanceCriteria: p95 response latency remains at or below 250 ms at the reference load.

assumptions.statement: The existing database supports additive schema changes.
assumptions.validationApproach: Inspect the deployed database version and migration policy before finalizing the migration task.

unknowns.description: The production p95 latency baseline is not yet supplied.
unknowns.impact: The target may be too strict or too lenient for the actual workload.
unknowns.resolutionApproach: Measure the current p95 under a representative load before setting the release threshold.

constraints: Raw credentials must not be included in the plan or repository.

components.name: Inventory API
responsibilities: Expose item lookup and stock adjustment contracts.
Validate request data and map domain outcomes to API responses.

decisions.decision: Keep stock adjustment rules in a domain service.
decisions.reason: The rules should not be duplicated across transport handlers.
alternatives: Implement rules directly in route handlers

dataFlows.description: Request and response exchange over the documented API.

tasks.title: Define inventory API contracts
tasks.description: Specify lookup and stock-adjustment request/response contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract defines success, validation, and not-found response shapes.
The stock-adjustment schema requires a reason and quantity delta.

tasks.title: Design inventory domain rules
tasks.description: Document quantity validation and adjustment invariants against the API contract.
acceptanceCriteria: The domain rules define allowed and rejected adjustment cases.
Every rule is traceable to REQ-002.

tasks.title: Specify API acceptance scenarios
tasks.description: Map contract and domain rules to observable acceptance scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: Scenarios cover known and unknown item lookup.
Scenarios cover valid and invalid stock adjustments.

risks.description: Unspecified identity provider may affect authentication integration design.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the identity provider and claims contract before provider-specific planning.

evidence.description: Inventory API request supplied for this example.

clarifications.question: Which identity provider and authorization claims should the API use?

testStrategy.approach: Risk-based layered verification planned before implementation.
entryCriteria: API contract and threat assumptions are reviewed.
exitCriteria: Planned checks have passed in the implementation environment and their evidence has been reviewed.
testStrategy.testData: Synthetic records with tenant-boundary and pagination edge cases.

rollbackPlan.rationale: The proposed change alters a deployed API and persisted data path.
rollbackPlan.strategy: Use an additive deployment and preserve the prior API contract until the new path is accepted.
triggerConditions: Error rate or p95 latency exceeds the agreed release guardrail.
steps: Route traffic back to the previous compatible path.
Reconcile writes using the documented idempotent procedure.
verification: Confirm health indicators return to the agreed baseline.
Confirm no accepted writes are lost or duplicated.
rollbackPlan.dataCompatibility: New writes must remain readable by the previous version for the rollback window; validate this assumption before release.
